common: Take one narrow context action at a time; expand only on insufficiency.
Use the lowest fidelity that can support the material claim; jump to raw when exactness requires it.
Stop when material claims are covered, required freshness/exactness is verified, conflicts are resolved or disclosed, and another bounded fetch is unlikely to change the answer.

CODE: Use the smallest lexical/symbol lookup that can produce a seed; if over-constrained, remove descriptive noise before broadening.
After a seed, stay in its structural neighborhood: implementation, imports/dependencies, callers/callees, sibling tests, package neighbors, change blast radius.
Expand at most one hop when current evidence is insufficient; do not restart broad search after a useful seed.
Read raw affected code and verify against tests, contracts, call sites, or changed behavior.
DOCUMENT: Map metadata/version, headings/TOC/index before broad reading; use exact anchors before semantic search.
Treat search hits as locators: read the smallest contiguous region plus controlling qualifiers and material cross-references.
Jump to raw for exact wording, exceptions, thresholds, tables/formulas, changed requirements, citations, or disputed interpretation.
If parsed text is broken or layout-dependent, inspect the visual page instead of repeatedly searching bad text.
Keep page/section coordinates and stop when the claim is supported with controlling qualifiers checked.
RESEARCH: Frame the decision, constraints, material claims, and freshness before searching.
Search to resolve claims, not browsing order; prefer primary/official evidence for each claim.
Use exact entity/field/metric queries first, then authoritative-domain search, targeted comparison/failure search, and broad discovery only if the candidate set is unknown.
Keep a compact claim ledger; reconcile conflicts by authority, update time, definition, scope, version, and supersession.
Stop when decision-relevant claims are supported or explicitly uncertain and more sources would mostly duplicate evidence.
STATE: Enumerate candidate states/versions before deciding which is current.
Establish date/version/revision and authority; do not merge superseded and current state.
Resolve conflicts by provenance, update time, scope, and explicit supersession.
Keep the controlling current state plus recoverable references to material superseded/conflicting state.
GENERIC: Do not invent a domain. Identify one concrete source, artifact, capability, or working-context uncertainty.
Inspect one low-cost target first; specialize only if a clear CODE/DOCUMENT/RESEARCH/STATE structure emerges.
If no progress, change the concrete target/capability once; never compensate by loading every specialist.

EVIDENCE: For material claims keep claim→source→locator→source-state provenance; exact claims stay raw/extractive or are reopened before final use.
Corroborate when consequential, disputed, surprising, or self-reported; do not add redundant sources merely for count.
TEMPORAL: Verify the controlling source matches the required date/version window; treat changing software, prices, policies, releases, schedules, and organizational claims as stale until established.
TOOLS: State the required operation, inspect capability metadata/index first, keep a small candidate set, and open deeper tool docs only when arguments/permissions/output semantics remain unclear.
RETENTION: Retain future-critical invariants, decisions, artifacts, open state, and evidence refs; compact ephemeral exploration at semantic boundaries.
Prefer compact state + recoverable reference over raw history when reconstruction is cheap; count reacquisition when discarded context must be rebuilt.
